title: Attention heuristics profiling and span boundaries for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Track and expose attention pathway decision points and their timing to improve prefill/decode scheduler decisions. Instrument attention heuristic exits, key/kernel selection gates, and span boundaries so scheduling can attribute latency to decision branches (e.g., fused attention vs. fallback). Deliver NVTX ranges, explicit span anchors, and per-kernel timing columns consumable by the console and perf dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Attention decision points emit named spans with stable hierarchy and <5% overhead on p99 latency for baseline workload
Prefill/decode scheduler gets an API to read recent attention-pathway hot counts and mean latencies
Dashboard shows breakdowns by heuristic (fused, split-attn, causal fallback) for last 24h and for selected model-version
Unit and e2e tests validate span naming, ordering, and fallback attribution
implementation_plan: Add lightweight attention 'decision' markers around kernel selection in attention runner
Map decision markers to NVTX ranges with deterministic names and attributes (model, seq_len, heuristic)
Expose a rolling counter/latency histogram from runtime to export to metrics endpoint
Add scheduler hook to consume metrics and adjust prefetch/batch thresholds in canary
Create console visualization prototype and perf-dashboard panels

tradeoffs: Adding spans increases instrumentation overhead; we will keep decision spans minimal and sample at 1% by default
Exposing per-heuristic histograms increases cardinality for metrics; to control cost we will roll up to heuristic names and seq-length buckets
Tighter coupling between scheduler and telemetry may reduce decoupling; use a read-only metrics API surface to avoid strong runtime deps
open_questions: What is safe default sampling rate for production? (1% vs 0.1%)
Should we record exact kernel arg sizes (embedding dimension) in spans or only bucketize?
How to surface these metrics for Private deployments without leaking model metadata?
design_decisions: Sample runtime spans at 1% by default and provide per-tenant override
Metric rollups will use seq_len buckets: small(<=128), med(129-512), large(>512)
risks: High-cardinality metrics across many model versions
NVTX payloads affecting NVTX collector overhead
next_steps: Finalize sampling config and add tenant opt-in flag
Implement histogram export and add scheduler consumer API
Create console panels and PRDs for rollout canary
